blocks.title: Resources
blocks.md: **Natural resources** are useful things from nature: **fertile soil** for crops, **forests** for timber, **rivers** for fish and **hydroelectric power**, the **sea** for fish and ports, and **petroleum**. Cameroon sells **raw materials** such as cocoa, coffee, cotton, timber and bananas to other countries.

blocks.caption: Natural resources and their uses.
blocks.alt: A table of natural resources and uses: fertile soil for cocoa, coffee, bananas and food crops; forests for timber, firewood and wildlife; rivers for fish, water and electric power; petroleum offshore sold abroad; sea and ports for fishing and trade.

blocks.title: Industries
blocks.md: **Industries** turn raw materials into goods. Examples: **cocoa beans** into chocolate, **cotton** into cloth, **palm nuts** into oil, **logs** into planks, **sugar cane** into sugar. This is called **processing**. Processed goods sell for **more money** than raw ones and give people **jobs**. Many factories are in **Douala**, the biggest port and city.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Thinking that a resource lasts forever: forests, soil and fish must be protected.
- Saying that only farming is important: industry, trade and services matter too.
- Calling cocoa beans a manufactured good: they are raw materials; chocolate is manufactured.
- Believing that natural resources are the same in every region.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Sort into raw materials or manufactured goods: cotton, cloth, cocoa beans, chocolate.
steps: Cotton and cocoa beans come straight from the farm: raw materials.
Cloth and chocolate are made in factories: manufactured goods.
blocks.answer: Raw: cotton, cocoa beans; manufactured: cloth, chocolate.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: A farmer sells 800 kg of cocoa beans at 1,000 FCFA per kg. A factory sells the same weight of processed cocoa products at 2,500 FCFA per kg. How much more money does the processed cocoa bring?

blocks.title: Rural and urban
blocks.md: A **rural** area is the countryside: villages with farms, forests and few services. An **urban** area is a town or **city**: many people, houses, shops, schools, hospitals, offices, factories and busy roads. **Yaoundé** and **Douala** are Cameroon's biggest cities; **Bamenda**, **Bafoussam**, **Garoua**, **Maroua**, **Buea** and **Limbe** are other well-known towns.

blocks.caption: Village, town and city.
blocks.alt: Three boxes: village with farming, fishing and quiet; town with markets, shops and schools; city with factories, ports and jobs.

blocks.title: Why towns grow, and rural-urban migration
blocks.md: Towns grow where there are **ports** (Douala), **roads and railways**, **good soil** and **water**, **markets** and **administration** (Yaoundé). Many people move from villages to cities for **jobs, schools and hospitals**: this is **rural-urban migration**. Cities have **opportunities**, but also **crowding, traffic, rubbish and high rents**. Villages need good roads, schools and clinics so that people can also live well there.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Thinking that cities have only advantages (or only problems).
- Looking down on village life: farmers feed the country.
- Throwing rubbish in drains and streets in towns.
- Saying that Douala is the capital: it is Yaoundé.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Give two reasons why people move from villages to cities.
steps: Cities offer more jobs and more schools.
They also have hospitals and other services.
blocks.answer: For jobs and for schools and hospitals.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Give one problem of a growing city.
steps: Many people live in a small area.
Traffic jams, rubbish and crowded housing are problems.
blocks.answer: For example traffic jams and rubbish.
